## Micro, macro and alternatives

Micro: existing portal builder and web assets were a documentation landing, without the requested House-first flow or PWA manifest/service worker. Macro: preserve all legal chapters, appendix downloads, public-file digests, exact-byte evidence approvals and disabled findings publication. Reuse and enhance those assets rather than create a parallel investigator app. A full live API or open tip form would exceed the validated infrastructure and distract from the representative's first task; those remain separate roadmap gates.

## Assumption audit and decision

The owner-private preview contains reviewed public methods, not private case data. Publishing it does not contact legislators or change the audience to public. Wrongly implying official authority, complete runtime autonomy or anonymity is a high-impact failure; the interface labels proposed actions and closed intake, supplies no sensitive input, and keeps agent services explicitly planned. Cache expansion could retain inappropriate content; the service worker allowlists shell resources and rejects arbitrary API/external caching. Decision: proceed with the bounded owner-private prototype; no public sharing change, confidential intake or autonomous activation.
